banana_peel.immediate_action: Compost at home or place in the appropriate wet-waste stream

alternatives.name: Home Composting
procedure: Cut the banana peel into smaller pieces.
Add it to a suitable home composting system.
Mix or cover it with suitable dry brown material.
Maintain appropriate moisture and aeration as the compost develops.
alternatives.benefit: Helps divert organic waste from disposal and produces compost that can be used as a soil amendment.

alternatives.name: Vermicomposting
procedure: Cut the banana peel into smaller pieces.
Add a moderate amount to an established vermicomposting system.
Cover it with suitable bedding material.
Maintain suitable moisture and conditions for the worms.
alternatives.benefit: Converts suitable organic waste into worm castings that can be used to improve soil.

alternatives.name: Use Finished Compost as Soil Amendment
procedure: Compost the banana peel with other suitable organic materials.
Allow the composting process to finish completely.
Mix the finished compost into garden soil as a soil amendment.
alternatives.benefit: Returns organic matter to the soil and can improve soil structure and moisture retention.

banana_peel.safety_note: Use clean banana peels and follow appropriate composting practices.

vegetable_scraps.immediate_action: Compost at home or place in the appropriate wet-waste stream

alternatives.name: Home Composting
procedure: Collect suitable vegetable scraps and remove any non-compostable material.
Cut larger pieces into smaller pieces.
Add the scraps to a suitable composting system.
Balance the material with suitable dry brown material and maintain moisture and aeration.
alternatives.benefit: Diverts suitable organic waste from disposal and produces compost for use as a soil amendment.

alternatives.name: Vermicomposting
procedure: Remove unsuitable materials from the vegetable scraps.
Cut larger scraps into smaller pieces.
Add a moderate amount to an established vermicomposting system.
Cover the scraps with suitable bedding material and maintain appropriate conditions.
alternatives.benefit: Converts suitable vegetable waste into worm castings that can be used to improve soil.

alternatives.name: Vegetable Stock
procedure: Select clean vegetable trimmings that are suitable for food use.
Wash the trimmings appropriately.
Simmer suitable trimmings in water to prepare stock.
Discard any remaining material through the appropriate organic-waste route.
alternatives.benefit: Can extend the useful life of suitable food material and reduce avoidable food waste.

vegetable_scraps.safety_note: Only use clean, food-safe scraps for food preparation. Do not use spoiled, moldy, or contaminated material.

paper.immediate_action: Reuse if possible; otherwise keep clean and dry for appropriate paper recycling

alternatives.name: Reuse Blank Sides
procedure: Check whether the paper has a clean and usable side.
Reuse the blank side for notes, drafts, or other suitable purposes.
alternatives.benefit: Extends the useful life of the paper before recycling or disposal.

alternatives.name: Paper Crafts
procedure: Select clean and suitable paper.
Cut, fold, or combine it to create simple educational or craft materials.
alternatives.benefit: Repurposes usable paper and delays disposal.

alternatives.name: Composting Suitable Paper
procedure: Use only suitable non-glossy and minimally treated paper.
Shred the paper into smaller pieces.
Add it as a dry brown material to a suitable composting system.
alternatives.benefit: Allows suitable paper to contribute carbon-rich material to a composting process.

paper.safety_note: Keep recyclable paper clean and dry. Avoid composting glossy, laminated, heavily coated, or contaminated paper.

cardboard_box.immediate_action: Reuse if possible; otherwise flatten and keep dry for appropriate paper/cardboard recycling

alternatives.name: Storage Organizer
procedure: Clean and inspect the cardboard box.
Reuse it to store lightweight household, study, or office items.
alternatives.benefit: Extends the useful life of the cardboard and reduces the need for new storage materials.

alternatives.name: Packaging Material
procedure: Check that the box is clean and structurally sound.
Reuse it for suitable packing or transporting items.
alternatives.benefit: Reduces the need for new packaging material.

alternatives.name: Composting Suitable Cardboard
procedure: Remove tape, plastic, labels, and other unsuitable materials.
Use only suitable untreated cardboard.
Shred or tear it into smaller pieces.
Add it as dry brown material to a suitable composting system.
alternatives.benefit: Allows suitable cardboard to contribute carbon-rich material to compost.

cardboard_box.safety_note: Avoid composting waxed, laminated, heavily treated, or contaminated cardboard.

plastic_bottle.immediate_action: Empty, rinse if appropriate, and send for suitable plastic recycling or recovery

alternatives.name: Reuse for Suitable Storage
procedure: Clean the bottle thoroughly.
Reuse it only for a suitable non-hazardous purpose.
alternatives.benefit: Extends the useful life of the bottle before recycling.

alternatives.name: Plant or Seedling Container
procedure: Clean the bottle.
Prepare it carefully for use as a small plant or seedling container.
Ensure suitable drainage and safe handling of any cut edges.
alternatives.benefit: Repurposes a used container for a practical household or gardening use.

alternatives.name: Plastic Recycling
procedure: Empty the bottle and clean it where appropriate.
Separate it according to the local waste-collection requirements.
Place it in the appropriate plastic recycling or recovery stream.
alternatives.benefit: Allows suitable plastic material to enter an appropriate recovery or recycling pathway.

plastic_bottle.safety_note: Do not use damaged plastic bottles for hot liquids or unsuitable food storage. Follow local recycling requirements.

flexible_food_packet.immediate_action: Keep clean and dry and use the appropriate flexible-packaging collection or recovery route

alternatives.name: Craft or Organization Material
procedure: Empty and clean the packet as far as practical.
Reuse the material for simple craft or organization purposes where appropriate.
alternatives.benefit: Repurposes packaging material and delays disposal.

alternatives.name: Flexible Packaging Recovery
procedure: Empty the packet and remove remaining food material.
Keep the packaging clean and dry where possible.
Use a local collection or recovery route that accepts the specific type of flexible packaging.
alternatives.benefit: Directs suitable flexible packaging toward an appropriate recovery pathway.

flexible_food_packet.safety_note: Do not compost flexible food packets or place them in paper recycling. Acceptance of flexible packaging varies by local collection systems.

pen_stationery.immediate_action: Check whether the item can be refilled or repurposed before disposal

alternatives.name: Refill Compatible Pen
procedure: Check whether the pen is designed to accept a compatible replacement refill.
Replace the empty refill with a suitable compatible refill.
Continue using the pen if it remains functional.
alternatives.benefit: Extends the useful life of the pen and reduces the need to discard the pen body.

alternatives.name: Creative or Educational Reuse
procedure: Clean the stationery item where appropriate.
Reuse suitable components for simple craft, educational, or organizational activities.
alternatives.benefit: Repurposes suitable stationery components and delays disposal.

alternatives.name: Appropriate Disposal
procedure: If the pen cannot be refilled or repurposed, keep it separate from organic waste.
Follow the appropriate local waste-collection or disposal route.
alternatives.benefit: Ensures the item is directed toward the appropriate waste pathway when further reuse is not practical.

pen_stationery.safety_note: Do not cut, burn, or heat stationery items to recover materials. Recycling acceptance varies by local facility.

electrical_wire.immediate_action: Keep separate and send to an authorized e-waste collection or recycling channel

alternatives.name: Authorized E-waste Recovery
procedure: Keep the wire separate from ordinary household waste.
Do not burn or strip the insulation at home.
Send it to an authorized e-waste collection or recycling channel.
alternatives.benefit: Allows electrical materials to enter a more appropriate recovery pathway.

electrical_wire.safety_note: Do not burn insulation, strip wires using unsafe methods, or perform electrical work unless you are qualified to do so.

battery.immediate_action: Keep separate from ordinary waste and take it to an appropriate battery collection or recycling point

alternatives.name: Battery Collection and Recycling
procedure: Keep the battery separate from ordinary household waste.
Do not open, puncture, crush, burn, or modify the battery.
Take it to an appropriate battery collection or recycling point.
alternatives.benefit: Supports safe handling and recovery of materials from used batteries.

battery.safety_note: Never open, puncture, crush, burn, short-circuit, or modify a battery. Follow the collection instructions for the specific battery type.

medicine_strip.immediate_action: Do not place unused or expired medicines in ordinary household waste; use an appropriate medicine take-back or disposal pathway

alternatives.name: Medicine Take-back or Authorized Disposal
procedure: Keep unused or expired medicines separate from ordinary waste.
Follow the instructions of an authorized medicine take-back or disposal facility where available.
Follow the applicable local guidance for medicine disposal.
alternatives.benefit: Reduces the risk of inappropriate disposal and supports safer handling of unused or expired medicines.

medicine_strip.safety_note: Do not reuse expired or unwanted medicines. Do not open, crush, burn, or repurpose medicine packaging for food or other household uses.

used_syringe.immediate_action: Do not place loose sharps in ordinary household waste; use an appropriate sharps or biomedical-waste disposal channel

alternatives.name: Safe Sharps Disposal
procedure: Do not bend, break, or manipulate the used needle unnecessarily.
Do not place the loose sharp in ordinary household waste or recycling.
Use an appropriate sharps container or disposal channel according to local medical-waste guidance.
alternatives.benefit: Reduces the risk of injury and supports safer handling of used sharps.

used_syringe.safety_note: Used needles can cause serious injury and infection risks. Never reuse or place loose needles in recycling or ordinary household waste.

sanitary_pad.immediate_action: Wrap securely and place in the appropriate sanitary-waste disposal stream

alternatives.name: Safe Sanitary-Waste Disposal
procedure: Wrap the used sanitary pad securely using suitable wrapping material.
Place it in the designated sanitary-waste or residual-waste stream according to local municipal guidance.
Do not place used sanitary products loose in recycling or composting.
alternatives.benefit: Supports hygienic handling and reduces exposure to contaminated waste.

sanitary_pad.safety_note: Do not wash, reuse, compost, or place disposable sanitary pads in ordinary recyclable-material streams.
